action: Swedbank Latvia advises customers not to trust suspicious texts, calls or emails asking for credentials or codes, as it told LETA (relayed by ERR).
date_note: Day ERR (BNS) published Cybernews' finding; ERR says Cybernews found the database on 28 September and gives no earlier public disclosure day; the Cybernews original could not be read.
exec: A Baltic SMS supplier's unprotected database held years of bank codes and sensitive texts from dozens of clients; banks are investigating their exposure.
geo_basis: victim country (CSC Telecom's Latvian branch, as ERR states)
impact: More than 125 million text messages were in the unprotected database, according to Cybernews as relayed by ERR and Escudo Digital. That is a count of messages, not of people. No page read says the data was misused.
plain: Researchers at Cybernews found an unprotected database at CSC Telecom's Latvian branch with more than 125 million text messages, including bank login codes and temporary passwords. Swedbank Latvia stopped using the supplier.

evidence.quote: CSC Telecomi turvanõrkus jättis kaitsmata andmebaasi, mis sisaldas enam kui 125 miljonit tekstisõnumit.
A major security breach has exposed more than 125 million SMS messages

summary: Cybernews found an unprotected database at CSC Telecom's Latvian branch holding more than 125 million SMS messages from October 2022 to September 2026, including authentication codes and temporary passwords, ERR and Escudo Digital report. Swedbank Latvia told LETA it suspended the provider; SEB said it used it only for pension-fund marketing. Latvia's Cert.lv asked CSC Telecom to investigate and informed law enforcement.
title: CSC Telecom Latvia database exposed years of SMS messages, Cybernews finds

validation.note: ERR (BNS) and Escudo Digital (14 Nov) both relay Cybernews' finding, one origin, so single_source; ERR adds statements by Swedbank Latvia, SEB and Cert.lv given to LETA. Cybernews original and DataBreaches.net answered 403; the Privacy Guides roundup was dropped as a source. No CSC Telecom confirmation of the Latvian exposure read, so status developing.

review.note: Roundup says 'over 125 million' SMS; record said about 125 million; fixed in impact, plain, summary. Single aggregator source (original Cybernews not read), so status rests on the roundup relaying the company's acknowledgement
